subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (Hosted API vs current provider) \u00101 post-call recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (Hosted API vs current provider) 1 post-call recap

Hi Alex / Samantha 1

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we9re all aligned.

Key performance targets (as discussed):
- p95 end-to-end latency: <= 200 ms (user-facing)
- p99 end-to-end latency: <= 450 ms (user-facing)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 requests/sec
- Peak concurrency: ~100 concurrent inferences (short bursts up to 200)
- Streaming requirement: yes 1 partial tokens should start rendering within ~5080 ms and keep steady chunking without long tail stalls
- Typical prompt/response: average 300 tokens input, ~150 tokens output; some longer sessions up to 1024 tokens

Current provider numbers you mentioned on the call: p95 ~320 ms, p99 ~980 ms (these are the pain points you want to remove). Primary symptoms: p99 spikes and delayed first-byte streaming when concurrency increases.

What Redwood can do / immediate plan:
1) Run an initial hosted benchmark against a dedicated test tenant using your representative query set and concurrency pattern. We9ll measure p50/p95/p99, first-byte streaming latency, and end-to-end (client-to-client) numbers.
2) Share an SLO measurement spec and a short script you can run locally to capture traces 1 this helps normalize comparisons vs your current provider.
3) If benchmarks look good, we9ll propose a short pilot (24 weeks) on Hosted API with a canary routing policy so you can validate in your environment.

Requested items from Finlytics to start the benchmark:
- Representative request set (CSV or sample requests) 1 includes token sizes and any multi-turn state.
- Typical concurrency profile (ramp up, steady-state, burst frequency).
- A short capture of current provider traces (p95/p99 & histograms) or access to the telemetry you referenced.
- Any security requirements for a hosted test tenant (IP allowlists, data residency constraints).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You share the sample request set and traces by EOD Tue (2027-06-08).
- Redwood runs a 2-day benchmark (Wed10) and returns the report + raw measurements.
- Quick sync to review results and agree on pilot (Fri).

Attaching a one-page SLO summary and an example CSV template for the request set. Let us know if you9d prefer Redwood runs a side-by-side test against your current provider (we can do that with your scripts/telemetry).

Thanks 1 I9ll loop in Marissa and Aditya to own the test execution.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270605-finlytics-slo-summary.pdf (summary, 1 page)
Attachment: finlytics-kpis.csv (sample request set template)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (Hosted API vs current provider) 1 post-call recap

Laura 1 thanks for the concise recap. Confirming a few items and a couple clarifying points: 

- We can provide the sample request set and current-provider traces. I9ll send the CSV + p95/p99 histograms by EOD Tue (2027-06-08).
- Current observed numbers (from our telemetry): p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 ~ 980 ms, p50 ~ 110 ms. The biggest user complaints are occasional long tail freezes during streaming (first-byte latency spikes).
- Concurrency profile: steady state ~100 concurrent, short bursts 12x for ~3090s.
- We prefer a side-by-side comparison run if possible 1 it helps our SREs trust the numbers. Can you run the benchmark against both Redwood Hosted and our current provider using the same workload?

Also important for procurement: we9ll need a short security checklist/NDA to allow the hosted test tenant to receive sample data. Do you have a template?

Appreciate the plan 1 looking forward to the benchmark.

1 Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform
Finlytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets (Hosted API vs current provider) 1 post-call recap

Hi Alex 1 looping in the engineering plan and exact inputs we9ll need to execute the side-by-side test. Thanks for sending the CSV/traces tomorrow 1 that will let us normalize the workload.

Redwood test plan (high level):
1) Normalize the workload: run your provided CSV through our generator to replicate token distributions and multi-turn flows.
2) Run parallel benchmarks: (a) hosted Redwood test tenant (dedicated capacity), (b) your current provider endpoint 1 same request stream, same concurrency pattern.
3) Metrics captured: client-to-client end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), first-byte streaming latency, throughput (req/s), successful chunk rate for streaming, and error rates.
4) We9ll capture raw traces and provide histogram exports + CSVs so you can ingest them into your telemetry.

Inputs we need from Finlytics: 
- The CSV/sample requests (tokens per request indicated).
- A short script or description of your concurrency ramp (we can also mimic based on the profile you sent).
- If you want side-by-side against your provider, well need either (a) a throwaway API key/endpoints to execute the provider side, or (b) you run the provider-side run and share traces (either is fine).
- Security: we can accept the data as anonymized samples. If you need an NDA, I9ve attached our standard test NDA and a security checklist 1 we can sign that quickly.

Timeline proposal (flexible):
- Tue 2027-06-08: receive CSV + traces + any provider endpoint (if you want us to run both sides).
- Wed10: Redwood runs parallel benchmarks and collects traces.
- Fri 2027-06-11: deliverable 1 benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 comparisons, streaming first-byte latency plots, and recommendations (batching/quantization/config changes).

If that works, well schedule a 30-min sync on Fri to walk the results.

Attaching: Redwood test NDA (template) and the one-page SLO summary you saw earlier.

Thanks,
Marissa (on behalf of the engineering bench)
